native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among NLSY79 respondents ever incarcerated between 1985 and 1994 (n=289), median 1985 wealth was very low overall (720 USD; 45.0% with net wealth <=0) and starkly stratified by race and sex: white incarcerated respondents had median 2,200 USD vs 320 USD for Black and 0 USD for Hispanic respondents (~7x gap), and incarcerated women had median 0 USD (70.3% <=0) vs 1,000 USD for men. In the race-by-sex cross-tabulation, white respondents held the highest medians (white women 4,100 USD; white men 2,000 USD), whereas Black women (n=16) and Hispanic women (n=9, unreliable small cell) had median 0 USD with Q3=0, meaning most had no positive net wealth. Context (not central): the ever-incarcerated median (720 USD) was one-fifth of the non-incarcerated median (3,600 USD). Temporal caveat: ever_jailed spans 1985-1994, so 1985 wealth may precede or follow incarceration for different individuals; findings are descriptive, not causal.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows, 0 missing); normalized 'hipanic'->'hispanic'; filtered ever_jailed=1 (n=289); computed n, median, IQR, mean, pct wealth<=0, n_negative, min, max for the full jailed group, by race, by sex, and by race x sex (6 cells), plus context rows for ever_jailed=0 and full sample; medians used as primary statistic (robust to heavy right skew, range [-57,587; 2,574,706]); negative values kept as valid net wealth; no winsorization or exclusion; hispanic x female cell (n=9) flagged as unreliable; results exported to CSV and used to formulate a descriptive, non-causal natural-language hypothesis.
